markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Benign (90%)** · Ambiguous: Normal vs Benign · Careful review
Conformal set holds Normal and Benign; invasive probability is under 1% [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Benign 90%, Normal 7%, InSitu 3% | Benign clearly leads |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90% level) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.94 / 84th percentile | No quality flag raised |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Yes, same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 2 of 5 Benign | Weak neighbor support |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 2, 6, 7) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; spot check failed, so not a reason [F2] · Unreliable
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 0, 4, 7) · ↓ invasive · Modestly above typical; fits benign tissue · Validated
- **Nuclei segmentation** (regions 6, 7, 8) · ↓ invasive · No neoplastic nuclei in three sampled regions · Measured
- **Tumor infiltrating stroma** (region 0) · ↓ invasive · Near-typical score; small downward contribution here · Validated

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions lowers the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful.
- **Concepts**: Deletion difference 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0; not shown to reflect the classifier. This case leans on normal lobules and mitoses, both 0/20, Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Normal and Benign overlap; the 90% guarantee cannot separate them.
- Few similar cases agree (2 of 5), and sampled nuclei contained no epithelium.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 2, 6, 7:** confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; this concept failed its spot check.
2. **Region 6:** highest per-region invasive probability (5%); confirm no stromal invasion.
3. **Region 0:** strongest tumor-infiltrating-stroma score; confirm stroma is benign.
